paper.title_en: Low-loss chip-to-free-space connectivity via hybrid Si-on-TFLN: efficient and scalable grating couplers for quantum SoC integration
paper.abstract_en: The “loss-budget” at optical I/O interfaces has become a primary bottleneck for scaling multi-node quantum networks and entanglement distribution. We demonstrate a high-efficiency, CMOS-compatible hybrid Siliconon- TFLN architecture designed to meet the rigorous demands of quantum system-on-chip (SoC) integration. By utilizing a high-index silicon overlay to enhance diffraction contrast, we eliminate parasitic losses from metallic reflectors and bypass the challenges of dry-etching TFLN for grating couplers. Our proposed platform achieves an experimental coupling efficiency of -2.1dB at 780nm, targeted for the D2 absorption line of 87Rb used in neutral atom quantum computing and atomic sensors and an efficiency of -1.24dB at 1520nm. The decoupling of the waveguide and grating fabrication enables the use of mature silicon processing to achieve 130nm smallest feature sizes with high fidelity, ensuring a scalable and fabrication-tolerant optical interface. This approach allows for unconstrained waveguide etch depths, facilitating the integration of active (χ(2)) components required for heralded photon generation and high-speed qubit manipulation. Experimental spectral data confirms a broad 3-dB bandwidth of approximately 40nm at 1520 nm, while the 780nm band provides the high-efficiency connectivity essential for chip-scale atomic clocks and precision spectroscopy. By significantly reducing interface losses without complex additive processes, this demonstration paves the way for efficient frequency conversion and scalable connectivity in next-generation quantum photonics.
